DisplayName: Emergency hotfix rollout with shard-risk governance
Summary: Emergency delivery template for time-critical production remediation with explicit containment, rollback, customer communication, artifact-input, and approval discipline aligned to the current process architecture.
ValueStatement: Restores service or mitigates incident impact quickly without disguising rollback, data, or customer communication risk.
InterfaceContractSummary: Emergency software delivery spans production operations, customer communication, database safety, and release governance, so the process must keep those boundaries explicit.
GovernanceNotes: Time pressure never removes the need for explicit rollback ownership, communication ownership, typed emergency evidence, or explicit dependency joins.
ChangeSummary: Refreshed to use current first-class dependencies and artifact inputs for emergency approval instead of compressing them into legacy single-edge sequencing.
GovernancePolicySummary: Emergency release requires typed blast-radius analysis, focused QA proof, release approval, and explicit rollback trigger ownership.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Command, communication, database safety, and rollout execution remain durable role contracts even if people on the rota change.
OperatingModeSummary: Emergency execution is allowed only inside a bounded release window with explicit rollback and communication obligations.
SimulationReadinessSummary: This template is intentionally rich enough for emergency simulation, incident replay, and canvas authoring validation.
Metrics: Median time from bridge activation to blast-radius assessment.
Emergency approvals with explicit rollback trigger and customer communication owner.
Rate of emergency rollouts completed without unplanned rollback.
Share of post-incident reviews completed with corrective actions and owners inside SLA.
Number of incidents where emergency scope expanded beyond the approved blast radius.
Risks: Emergency work expanding into an unreviewable normal release.
Rollback triggers unclear at the moment of production action.
Customer communication lagging behind operational state.
Database or shard-risk implications hidden inside platform-only notes.
Emergency approval proceeding without explicit artifact inputs.
TailoringRules: Minor operational mitigations that do not deploy code may use a reduced package step, but approval still requires explicit blast-radius and validation evidence.
If no data or shard state is touched, database review may downgrade from mandatory reviewer to optional reviewer with recorded rationale.
Where no shadow environment exists, validation may use the safest representative proving lane available, but skipped checks must be explicit.
Long-running or multi-service fixes must be moved out of the emergency lane into planned software delivery.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Drive containment and structured decision-making when time pressure and uncertainty are high.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior incident leader who can coordinate specialists, protect signal quality, and make time-sensitive trade-offs.
RoleUsages.Notes: Crisis-flow owner for coordination, decision timing, and containment during active incidents.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Provide the reliable platform path required to build, deploy, observe, and if necessary roll back changes safely.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A technical specialist in CI/CD, environments, infrastructure, and observability integration.
RoleUsages.Notes: Environment and delivery-pipeline owner for build integrity, deployment mechanics, and operational guardrails.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own emergency database diagnostics, hotfix compatibility assessment, and rollback trigger definition.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A hands-on production database specialist for emergency change paths.
RoleUsages.Notes: Specialist responder for shard, schema, and persistence hotfix risk.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Challenge whether the delivered change is proven enough for its risk profile and make test evidence decision-ready for release governance.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior test leader able to shape strategy, select evidence depth, and identify where automation is not enough.
RoleUsages.Notes: Quality owner for coverage depth, evidence quality, and release confidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Decide whether the accumulated evidence is sufficient to expose the change to real users, data, and operational load.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: A senior operational or governance authority who can accept release risk on behalf of the organization.
RoleUsages.Notes: Final go-live decision owner for production promotion and rollback preparedness.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Represent the customer communication path during release and incident work without allowing message drift from operational facts.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: Customer communication owner for service-impacting release or incident lanes.
RoleUsages.Notes: Customer communication owner for service-impacting release or incident lanes.

Steps.Title: Activate emergency bridge and classify severity
Steps.Subtitle: Command posture
Steps.Notes: Establish the incident bridge, initial severity, and named command boundaries before packaging a hotfix.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Active production signal, customer impact, and first-response telemetry.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit command bridge with severity posture, responder roster, and immediate constraints.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Bridge activation log, severity declaration, and named responders.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander owns classification and decision pacing during the emergency window.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not begin emergency packaging while command ownership or severity framing is still implicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Command ownership may rebind across rota changes, but the command contract remains explicit.
Customer communication owner tracks external impact from the start.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency bridge activation log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident timeline, hotfix approval, and post-incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must record activation time, severity, named responders, and first declared constraints.

Steps.Title: Assess blast radius and rollback constraints
Steps.Subtitle: Risk framing and bounded emergency scope
Steps.Notes: Determine which shards, data paths, tenants, and rollback constraints bound the emergency change.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Emergency bridge log, production telemetry, and known change hypotheses.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Explicit blast-radius assessment with rollback constraints and bounded emergency scope.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Impact map, rollback notes, and disallowed expansion paths.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander frames the boundary; platform and database owners challenge unsupported assumptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause immediately when the required fix grows into an unreviewable multi-area release.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency boundary ownership stays with command.
Platform owner reviews operational fit of the proposed emergency boundary.
Database review is mandatory where shard state or tenant data is affected.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Blast-radius assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for validation, release approval, and later incident review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must identify impacted shards or services, rollback constraints, and forbidden scope expansion paths.

Steps.Title: Package emergency hotfix and rollback scripts
Steps.Subtitle: Controlled change assembly
Steps.Notes: Assemble the emergency patch, deployment instructions, and rollback scripts under one accountable engineer.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Blast-radius assessment, target change scope, and deployment constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Hotfix package with rollout steps, rollback scripts, and changed-surface inventory.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Patch diff, deployment bundle, schema scripts, and operator checklist.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Platform engineer owns assembly but cannot expand scope beyond the approved emergency boundary.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Pause immediately when the required fix grows into an unreviewable multi-area release.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency packaging remains attached to the platform-engineer role even if the individual changes.
Database review is mandatory for scripts that touch shard state or tenant data.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency patch and rollback bundle
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for validation, release approval, and post-incident engineering review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must link the exact patch, database scripts, rollback path, and operator checklist.

Steps.Title: Validate emergency fix in shadow environment
Steps.Subtitle: Fast but explicit regression gate
Steps.Notes: Run the emergency checklist against the hotfix bundle in a shadow or representative environment before release approval.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Emergency patch bundle, known blast radius, and incident reproduction notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Focused validation result with residual risks and unsupported cases.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Checklist output, shadow-environment notes, and residual-risk annotations.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: QA responder may block the rollout if the emergency evidence is too thin for the risk profile.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not convert the gate into a verbal approval; evidence still needs typed reviewable form.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency QA ownership may move across the responder rota but the gate remains explicit.
Package owner reviews failures and unsupported coverage before approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency validation evidence pack
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for emergency release approval and later correction of the emergency checklist.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name validated flows, skipped checks, and residual risk that the approver must accept explicitly.

Steps.Title: Approve emergency release window
Steps.Subtitle: Explicit go / no-go and rollback trigger
Steps.Notes: Review the emergency evidence, rollback trigger, and customer communication plan before production rollout.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Validation evidence, rollback trigger, customer-impact status, and operator readiness.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Go / no-go decision with explicit rollback trigger and accountable owners.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Approval note, release window, fallback trigger, and outward-communication owner.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Release approver owns the emergency release decision and cannot waive missing evidence or unclear rollback control.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Reject the rollout when rollback conditions or customer-facing obligations are not explicit.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Emergency release approval remains attached to the role, not a specific operator.
Customer communication owner must review timing and outbound commitments before approval.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency release approval record
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for audit, customer follow-up review, and future emergency policy tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must name the approver, rollback trigger, communication owner, and residual risk owner.

Steps.Title: Execute emergency rollout and watch telemetry
Steps.Subtitle: Controlled production action
Steps.Notes: Roll out the patch inside the approved window while telemetry, shard locks, and customer communication remain actively managed.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved release record, deployment bundle, telemetry checkpoints, and customer message cadence.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Executed rollout with explicit telemetry outcome and rollback state.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Operator notes, telemetry checkpoints, rollback invocation if needed, and customer update timeline.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Platform engineer may execute only inside the approved window and rollback trigger boundaries.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Trigger rollback immediately when shard lock duration, tenant impact, or telemetry drift breaches the approved threshold.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Execution ownership remains with the platform-engineer role until rollout completes or fails.
Incident commander reviews telemetry and escalation timing throughout the rollout.
Database specialist remains an explicit fallback for rollback execution.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Emergency rollout and telemetry log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for incident replay and emergency policy tuning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture rollout timing, telemetry checkpoints, and any rollback invocation.

Steps.Title: Capture post-incident learning and corrective actions
Steps.Subtitle: Forensic replay and systemic follow-up
Steps.Notes: Turn the failed or recovered emergency path into explicit learning about detection, coordination, rollback, and architecture weaknesses.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Rollout outcome, telemetry record, customer communications, and command timeline.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Post-incident review with corrective actions, owner assignments, and simulation updates.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Timeline, contributing factors, missing controls, and next corrective actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Incident commander owns follow-up assignment while engineering and communications roles retain accountability for their control gaps.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not close the emergency process while corrective actions remain unnamed or unowned.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: The command role remains accountable until corrective actions have owners.
Engineering role reviews technical corrective actions.
Customer communication owner reviews trust and communication lessons.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Post-incident corrective action log
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for simulation packs, response playbook tuning, and recurring-incident analysis.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must capture missing controls, decision latency, and concrete corrective actions with owners.

LocalRoles.Summary: Owner for externally consistent status, workaround, and resolution messaging during hotfix execution.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Keep external communication factual, timely, and aligned with the current operational truth.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A customer-facing crisis communicator with authority to publish incident-safe customer updates.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Owner for externally consistent status, workaround, and resolution messaging during hotfix execution.
LocalRoles.SeniorityBand: Senior support or customer communications leadership
KnowledgeRequirements: Ability to turn volatile technical status into clear external messaging without overcommitting.
Knowledge of incident communication cadence, approval paths, and customer trust expectations.
Understanding of what technical detail is helpful, harmful, or unsafe to disclose externally.
Ability to maintain a single source of truth across support, account teams, and status channels.
Knowledge of workaround and ETA messaging practices during active incidents.
Ability to coordinate communication changes with the incident commander.
ExperienceRequirements: Has handled external messaging for an incident or high-severity outage.
Has coordinated communications with technical responders and customer-facing teams.
Has corrected or avoided inaccurate ETA commitments under pressure.
Has managed multi-audience incident updates with support or account teams.
Has captured communication lessons for future incident playbooks.
DecisionRights: Approve customer-facing incident or hotfix status language.
Block publication of unverified technical claims or unrealistic ETAs.
Escalate if internal facts are too weak to support promised resolution timing.
Decide when a workaround versus full-fix message should be published.
CollaborationExpectations: Coordinate with incident commander and customer success lead.
Keep support teams synchronized on approved language.
Use technical facts from responders without distorting them.
Feed customer confusion patterns back into incident review.
AntiPatterns: Publishing optimism as if it were evidence.
Letting every stakeholder improvise their own customer message.
Sharing technical hypotheses externally as confirmed facts.
Ignoring customer-action guidance while focusing only on root cause.
FitnessEvidence: Approved customer updates with clear timing and ownership.
Evidence of aligned support and customer-facing messaging.
Reduced confusion or escalation due to communication discipline.
Post-incident actions showing improvement of communication playbooks.

LocalRoles.Summary: Specialist responder for shard, schema, and persistence hotfix risk.
LocalRoles.Purpose: Own emergency database diagnostics, hotfix compatibility assessment, and rollback trigger definition.
LocalRoles.StaffingIntent: A hands-on production database specialist for emergency change paths.
LocalRoles.SnapshotSummary: Specialist responder for shard, schema, and persistence hotfix risk.
KnowledgeRequirements: Deep understanding of the live persistence topology, shard behavior, and emergency rollback constraints.
Knowledge of schema lock behavior, replication lag, and transaction-impact risk under emergency change.
Ability to assess whether a hotfix can be applied safely under ongoing incident pressure.
Understanding of forensic evidence needs while still containing customer impact.
Knowledge of telemetry required to detect silent data-side failure quickly.
Ability to design narrowly scoped emergency remediation paths.
ExperienceRequirements: Has supported emergency production changes affecting database or storage systems.
Has diagnosed live outage or degradation tied to schema or data-path behavior.
Has executed or aborted emergency change due to database safety signals.
Has documented rollback or compensating controls under severe time pressure.
Has worked with incident commanders on containment versus integrity trade-offs.
DecisionRights: Approve or block shard/database aspects of emergency rollout.
Define rollback trigger thresholds tied to persistence risk.
Escalate when the emergency path threatens data integrity.
Choose the least harmful containment path for database-specific risk.
CollaborationExpectations: Work directly with incident commander and platform engineer.
Provide concise risk summaries under pressure.
Coordinate with QA on data-path validation limits.
Preserve factual detail for the post-incident review.
AntiPatterns: Optimizing for service restoration while hiding integrity risk.
Guessing about shard behavior without reading live telemetry.
Treating rollback as trivial during emergency conditions.
FitnessEvidence: Emergency change notes with explicit risk and rollback triggers.
Evidence of incident support grounded in real telemetry.
Post-incident findings showing the role preserved integrity or accelerated diagnosis.
Operator trust in the role’s emergency judgments.

LocalArtifacts.Summary: Explicit rollback trigger sheet for emergency rollout that defines telemetry thresholds, shard-risk triggers, and stop conditions.
LocalArtifacts.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable only during the hotfix window, post-incident review, and authorized audit of the event.
LocalArtifacts.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must define concrete telemetry or operational signals, not vague discomfort language.

LocalChecklists.Summary: Ensures the emergency hotfix window has the minimum decision, communication, and rollback discipline.
LocalChecklists.EntryCriteria: A hotfix path has been chosen and the team is preparing to execute under incident conditions.
LocalChecklists.ExitCriteria: Rollback owner, communications path, watch coverage, and blast-radius framing are explicit.
Checks: Incident commander and hotfix specialists are assigned.
Rollback trigger sheet is available and understood.
Customer or stakeholder communication path is prepared.
First-hour telemetry watch owner is assigned.

LocalValidations.Summary: Confirms the hotfix remains narrowly scoped to the incident need and has not become an uncontrolled bundled release.
LocalValidations.PassCriteria: Hotfix scope is minimal, incident-linked, and clearly separable from unrelated backlog or convenience changes.
LocalValidations.FailCriteria: Emergency path includes unrelated opportunistic changes or unbounded side effects.
LocalValidations.EscalationRule: Escalate immediately and reset the hotfix scope before deployment.

LocalPrompts.Summary: Prompt scaffold for hotfix commander status briefs during the emergency window.
RefusalConditions: Refuse to state the hotfix is safe if the rollback trigger or blast radius is still unclear.
